name: Acinar Cell Carcinoma of the Pancreas

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Acinar Cell Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of tumor cells with acinar differentiation showing granular cytoplasm and formation of acinar structures
Positive immunostaining for pancreatic exocrine enzymes such as trypsin, chymotrypsin, and lipase
Identification of a pancreatic mass with solid and cystic components on CT or MRI
Symptoms consistent with pancreatic malignancy such as abdominal pain and weight loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of acinar differentiation with positive immunohistochemical staining for pancreatic enzymes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may assist but is not routinely required for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Characterized by subcutaneous fat necrosis and polyarthralgia

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal mass detected on physical examination

searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile
fat inflammation linked to pancreatic enzymes

laboratory: Elevated serum lipase and pancreatic enzymes
Mild anemia and elevated inflammatory markers
imaging: CT scan showing a well-defined pancreatic mass with mixed solid and cystic components
MRI demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement of the tumor
Possible biliary ductal dilatation if tumor obstructs bile duct
genetic: Somatic mutations in APC/β-catenin pathway genes in some cases
other: Histopathology revealing acinar differentiation with granular cytoplasm
Immunohistochemical positivity for trypsin, chymotrypsin, and lipase

distinguishingFeatures: Ductal adenocarcinoma shows glandular differentiation rather than acinar
Typically negative for pancreatic exocrine enzymes on immunohistochemistry
More common and associated with KRAS mutations
Neuroendocrine tumors express neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin, synaptophysin)

redFlags: Unexplained severe abdominal pain with weight loss
Signs of lipase hypersecretion syndrome such as panniculitis or polyarthralgia
references: WHO Classification of Tumours Editorial Board. WHO Classification of Tumours: Digestive System Tumours. 5th ed. IARC; 2019.
